title: Ramp and Block
intro: A toy car rolls down a ramp and bumps a block. Does the height of the ramp change how far the block moves?
note: This is a model that uses the lesson's backup numbers. Your own ramp trials in the lesson still count.
summary: A faster car moved the block farther: the low ramp moved it 2 to 3 cm and the high ramp 7 to 8 cm. The car's energy of motion moved to the block when they hit. Changing one thing at a time, and testing three times, made the result trustworthy.

rounds.question: Which ramp makes the toy car move the block farther?

factors.label: The toy car
factors.held: The same toy car each time
factors.why: If the car changes, the car could cause the difference, not the ramp height.

factors.label: The block target
factors.held: The same block, in the same spot
factors.why: If the block changes, the block could cause the difference, not the ramp height.

factors.label: How you let go
factors.held: Let the car go without pushing it
factors.why: If you push the car some times, your push could cause the difference, not the ramp.

rounds.measure: How far did the block move? (cm; bigger means more energy reached the block)

reads.q: Which ramp moved the block farther?

choices.label: The low ramp
choices.why: Compare the bars. The low ramp moved the block 2 to 3 cm. Is there a ramp with longer bars?

choices.label: The high ramp
choices.why: The high ramp moved the block 7 to 8 cm. The car was faster, so it pushed the block farther.

choices.label: They were the same
choices.why: The bars are not the same height. Look again.

reads.q: When the car hits the block, what happens to the car's energy of motion?

choices.label: Some of it moves to the block
choices.why: Yes. Before: the car moves. After: the block moves. Energy changed places.

choices.label: It disappears
choices.why: Energy does not just vanish. The block started to move, so where did that motion come from?

choices.label: The block makes new energy
choices.why: The block was still. It moved because the car hit it.

choices.label: the height of the ramp.
choices.why: Right. The ramp height was the one thing we changed.

choices.label: the size of the block.
choices.why: The block was held the same.

choices.label: the low ramp moved the block 7 to 8 cm.
choices.why: The low ramp moved it 2 to 3 cm.

choices.label: the high ramp moved the block 7 to 8 cm.
choices.why: Yes. That matches the high-ramp bars.

choices.label: the high ramp moved the block 2 to 3 cm.
a higher ramp makes the car faster, so it moves the block farther.
choices.why: Yes. A faster car carries more energy to the block.

choices.label: ramp height does not matter.
choices.why: The results are very different, so it matters.

choices.label: a lower ramp is faster.
choices.why: The low ramp moved the block less, so the car had less energy.
